persona.title: Persona

notFound.title: Persona not found
notFound.description: This persona no longer exists or is not available.

persona.blankTitle: You don't seem to have any persona.
persona.blankDescription: Create a reusable voice profile to apply consistent tone, vocabulary and brand context across your AI agents.

create.chooseMethod: How do you want to create this persona?
create.manualDesc: Fill in the persona's identity, style and guidelines yourself.
create.audioDesc: Upload a recording and let AI draft the persona for you to review.

validate.title: Validate content
validate.subtitle: Add documents, links or indexed content and score how well it fits this persona's audience.

dialogue.title: Persona dialogue
dialogue.subtitle: Pick a topic and two or more personas and watch them talk it through, turn by turn.
dialogue.setupDesc: Each persona must end every reply with a question, so the dialogue keeps flowing.
dialogue.needTwo: You need at least two speaker personas (SPEAKER or BOTH) to run a dialogue.
dialogue.topicPlaceholder: e.g. Should a startup adopt a four-day work week?
dialogue.speakersHint: Pick two or more — the number shows the speaking order.
dialogue.noLlm: No enabled LLM instance is available.

dashboard.configureHint: Identity, system instruction, style, guidelines and audience.
dashboard.chatHint: Talk to a chat that adopts this persona.
dashboard.validateHint: Score how well content fits this audience.
dashboard.systemInstructionHint: The system instruction prepended to chats that adopt this persona.
dashboard.notebookHint: Sources used to score content fit.
dashboard.fitReportHint: How well content matches this audience.

aiChat.panelSubtitle: Describe the voice and I'll draft the persona
aiChat.placeholder: e.g. A senior account executive voice for top-of-funnel demo prospects — concise, persuasive, asks one qualifying question at a time, never quotes prices in the first three turns.
aiChat.empty: Tell me who this persona should sound like — funnel stage, audience, tone — and I'll fill the form on the left.

fromAudio.drafted: Draft persona ready — review and save
fromAudio.failed: Could not derive a persona from the audio

match.title: Persona Match
match.subtitle: Group contents and personas into projects and see, in a matrix, what each content serves each persona for — and vice versa. The analysis runs periodically and re-tunes both sides.
match.emptyDescription: Create a group of contents and personas to generate the N×N report.
match.defaultSubtitle: Select contents and personas, and generate the N×N fit matrix.
match.newHeroSubtitle: Name the project. Then add contents and personas to generate the N×N matrix.
match.projectSectionDesc: Name and description of the analysis project.
match.contentsDesc: URL, indexed content or file. Added once per project — not per persona.
match.noContents: No content yet. Add the first one below.
match.personasDesc: Select the personas this project evaluates. The matrix is the product of contents × personas.
match.settingsDesc: Name, description and how often the analysis re-extracts the contents and recomputes the cells that changed.
match.resultsDesc: What each content serves each persona for — and what each persona serves each content for.
match.emptyPrompt: Add at least one content and one persona, then click Run analysis.
match.readyPrompt: {{count}} cells ready to evaluate ({{sources}} × {{personas}}). Click Run analysis.
match.nothingToAdjust: Nothing to adjust — content well aligned to this persona.
match.reportByContentSub: What each content serves each persona for.
match.reportByPersonaSub: What each persona serves each content for.
match.reportFooter: Report generated from the N×N fit matrix. Percentages combine deterministic readability and LLM evaluation.
match.validatePreparing: Preparing the fit matrix for {{name}} in Persona Match.

research.title: Synthetic User Research
research.subtitle: Interview a cohort of OCEAN-profiled personas over a protocol, then synthesize what they said into a thematic insights report with saturation scoring. A discovery co-pilot — it front-loads the problem space, it does not replace real users.
research.emptyDescription: Create a study — pick an audience of personas and an interview protocol — to generate a synthesized insights report.
research.newHeroSubtitle: Name the study and pick a protocol. Then add an audience of personas and run the cohort interviews.
research.studySectionDesc: Name, goal and interview protocol of the research study.
research.goalPlaceholder: What are we trying to learn from this audience?
research.defaultSubtitle: Pick an audience and a protocol, then run the cohort interviews.
research.protocolSectionDesc: How the cohort is interviewed, what the study is trying to learn, and which models run each stage.
research.hypothesisPlaceholder: What we expect to find — used to sharpen the interviewer.
research.conceptPlaceholder: The proposed concept, message or feature the synthetic users react to.
research.questionsPlaceholder: One question per line — asked verbatim, in order.
research.maxQuestionsHint: The adaptive interviewer stops here at the latest.
research.targetHint: Point the study at a live agent to have synthetic users test its real flow, tools and RAG.
research.audienceDesc: Select the personas to interview, in order. Each is interviewed independently over the protocol above.

program.title: Program rollup
program.subtitle: Plan several studies across different audiences and roll their insights up into one program view — the themes that recur across audiences surface here.
program.planDesc: Select the studies to roll up. Run any that haven't been run yet, then view the program view.
program.noStudies: No studies yet. Create a few research studies first.
program.unavailable: Nothing to roll up for the selected studies yet.
program.failed: Could not build the program rollup.
program.runFailed: Could not run all the selected studies.
program.rollupDesc: Totals across the selected studies and each study's sufficiency.
program.themesDesc: Themes aggregated across the program. Highlighted themes recur in more than one study.
program.noThemes: No themes were synthesized across these studies yet.

assistant.title: Research Assistant
assistant.desc: Not sure how to set it up? Describe what you want to learn and the assistant drafts a study you can edit before creating.
assistant.placeholder: e.g. I want to understand why trial users drop off before inviting their team.
assistant.drafted: Here's a study draft — review and edit the fields below, then create.
assistant.skippable: Optional — you can also fill the fields below directly and skip the assistant.
assistant.failed: Could not draft a study. Check that a default LLM is configured.

research.feedDesc: Run the cohort and watch each transcript land live. Expand an interview to read its questions and answers.
research.saveToRun: Save your changes before running the interviews.
research.needAudience: Add at least one persona to the audience to run.
research.feedEmpty: No interviews yet. Add an audience and click Run interviews.
research.reportDesc: The synthesized themes, verbatim participant quotes and recommendations — read by theme or by persona.
research.reportUnavailable: No insights yet. Run the interviews to synthesize a report.
research.saturationDesc: The honest sufficiency signal — as personas are interviewed in order, do marginal participants still raise new themes?
research.saturationUnavailable: Not enough interviews to score saturation yet.
research.notSaturated: Not saturated — later participants were still raising new themes.
research.conceptFitDesc: How the tested concept lands with each participant, scored through the shared content-fit evaluator.
research.conceptFitUnavailable: Concept fit is available once a concept-test study has been run.
research.graphDesc: Which participants cluster on which theme — the persona↔theme affinity derived from the report.
research.graphUnavailable: No theme graph yet. Run the interviews to synthesize themes.
research.driftDesc: How theme coverage moves across scheduled re-runs — one-shot research becoming continuous validation.
research.driftUnavailable: At least two runs are needed to show drift.
research.evalBridgeDesc: Promote this study's interviews into a reusable agent-QA dataset — a repeatable eval against this synthetic audience.
research.promoted: Promoted. The dataset is now available in the Eval Studio.
research.reportBrand: Viglet Turing ES · Synthetic User Research
research.reportFooter: Report synthesized from synthetic cohort interviews. A discovery co-pilot — validate with real users before acting.

cohort.title: Audience cohort synthesis
cohort.subtitle: Describe an audience in a paragraph and generate a diverse set of persona drafts — spread across the Big Five — ready to review, keep and interview.
cohort.briefDesc: One paragraph of demographics + psychographics. The cohort is drafted to span a real range of temperaments, not clones.
cohort.briefPlaceholder: e.g. Mid-market marketing managers in Brazil evaluating a new analytics tool — time-pressed, skeptical of hype, mixed technical depth.
cohort.neverSaved: Drafts are never saved automatically — keep the ones you want and refine them in the persona form.
cohort.failed: Could not synthesize the cohort. Check that a default LLM is configured.
cohort.reviewDesc: Keep a draft to open it in the persona form (edit + save), or discard it.
cohort.allDiscarded: All drafts discarded. Adjust the brief and synthesize again.

dialogueProject.title: Persona dialogue
dialogueProject.subtitle: Save dialogue projects — a topic and a roster of speaker personas — and watch them talk it through, turn by turn. Re-open and re-run any project.
dialogueProject.emptyDescription: Create a dialogue: pick a topic and two or more personas.
dialogueProject.defaultSubtitle: Set a topic and pick two or more speakers, then run the dialogue.
dialogueProject.newHeroSubtitle: Name the project. Then set a topic and pick the speakers.
dialogueProject.projectSectionDesc: Name and description of the dialogue project.
dialogueProject.topicPlaceholder: e.g. Should a startup adopt a four-day work week?
dialogueProject.speakersDesc: Pick two or more personas. The number shows the speaking order (round-robin).
dialogueProject.noSpeakers: No speaker personas available. Create SPEAKER or BOTH personas first.
dialogueProject.settingsDesc: The topic seeds the first turn; each persona must end every reply with a question so the dialogue keeps flowing.
dialogueProject.transcriptDesc: The live conversation. Re-running replaces it.
dialogueProject.transcriptEmpty: No conversation yet. Set a topic, pick speakers and run the dialogue.
dialogueProject.needTwo: Pick at least two speakers to run the dialogue.
dialogueProject.saveToRun: Save your changes to run the dialogue.
dialogueProject.turnsDesc: One round = every persona speaks once, in order — so nobody is left out.
